title: astra.registry.publisher/1
description: publishers/<owner>.json — what the registry knows about the ACCOUNT behind a listing, keyed by the GitHub owner of source.repo. Hand-written and hand-reviewed. Never derived from a bundle: a plugin's own manifest carries an `author` string the author typed, and a badge keyed on that would be forged by a one-line edit. The owner login is the only identity this registry proves, because it is what the ownership check binds to.

owner.description: The GitHub owner login, matching the file name. Compared case-insensitively against the owner half of every listing's source.repo.

display_name.description: What a person sees beside the badge. One record per publisher rather than a copy per listing, so a rename is one edit and two entries cannot disagree.

description_text.description: One line a PERSON reads beside the badge, saying who this publisher is to Astra — 'Main developer of Astra', not 'verified'. The tier says what kind of claim the registry is making; this says what the publisher actually is, which is the thing a user wanted to know. Reviewed like everything else in this file: it is free text rendered next to a trust mark, which is precisely where an impersonation would want to live, and the only thing standing in front of it is that a human wrote this line and a root-delegated key signed it.

tier.description:
A STRING and not a proto enum, deliberately — a new tier should cost a registry edit and a locale key, not a proto change and an arm in every shell. A client MUST render on explicit membership and never on a value being present or non-default.

`astra_team` and not `official`, because `official` is relative to nothing. Beside a plugin that plays DOOM or renders Bad Apple!!, a reader completes the sentence with the SUBJECT — "the official DOOM plugin", or worse, a claim on somebody else's rights. Naming Astra leaves nothing to complete: it says whose team, which is the only thing this tier ever meant.

verified_at.description: When the evidence below was first accepted.

last_confirmed_at.description: When it last held. Written by the re-check, not by hand.

expires_at.description: The backstop for a re-check that has been failing quietly. A record past this date is dropped from the index, so a tier nobody has confirmed inside the window lapses rather than persisting on the strength of having once been true. Required for `verified`; meaningless for `official`, whose evidence is a file in this repository.

evidence.description: WHY the tier holds, as a fact that can be re-checked later rather than a verdict recorded once. A tier granted and never revisited becomes a claim about who somebody used to be, and this registry is the only place that can notice.

oneOf.description: For `astra_team`: the account belongs to the project. Re-checkable by construction — the claim is this file, in this repository, and changing it is a reviewed commit.

proof.description: A URL on that domain serving the owner login. Re-fetched on a schedule; when it stops naming the owner, the tier is withdrawn.

oneOf.description: For `verified`: the publisher controls a domain that names them back. The evidence is live, so the badge can be taken away by the world changing rather than only by a person deciding.
